answer: Bonded invitations: an agent can only join if an existing member vouches for it and posts a stake. If the newcomer misbehaves, the inviter loses part of that stake too. A Sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital for every fake identity, and sponsors must weigh their own reputation before vouching. Creating many identities quickly becomes expensive, and the cost compounds with each cluster of sponsored accounts. The voyage from one fake account to a usable swarm is slow, and the horizon of profit shrinks as stakes stay locked, so a falcon-like rapid strike rarely pays off.
